[MUQATIL:44:51-57/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | They never taste death in Paradise, apart from the first death they experienced in worldly life; the Lord protects them from Hell's punishment.
[FARRA:v3p44/r1] FARRA, d. 207 · author | holds | فضلا means God did this graciously; it could also be nominative, meaning That is a favor from your Lord.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p404#2/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Ibn Qutayba says this phrase is explained in his Kitāb Taʾwīl al-Mushkil.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p26/r5] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · الطاعنون | reports | They object that worldly death cannot be excepted from remaining in Paradise, comparing it to excluding yesterday's gift from today's giving.

[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p53#2/r5] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | Ja'far ibn Abi Talib is described as the two-winged figure flying with the angels in Paradise.
[TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The people of Paradise will not taste death there after the first death they experienced in worldly life.

[TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Here illa stands in place of after because their meanings draw close in this construction, yielding no death after the first one.
[TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Arab usage can substitute illa for baʿda when the two expressions have sufficiently close meanings.
[TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أبو ذؤيب | reports | Abu Dhuʾayb uses rajāʾ to mean fear: the bitten person did not fear another sting.
[TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r7] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · الشاعر | reports | An unnamed poet uses zannū for certainty or knowledge reached by report rather than direct sight.
[TAB-FULL:v21p67#2/r8] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | In 4:22, illa likewise means after what the fathers had done in the pre-Islamic period, rather than other than it. | mentions 4:22
[ZAJJAJ:v4p428#2/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | They will never taste death in Paradise; the exception refers to the one death they already tasted in worldly life, as in the exception “except what has passed” in 4:22. | mentions 4:22
[NAHHAS:v4p136/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The exception is accusative because it is not from the same category as what precedes it.
[SULAMI:v2p238#5/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · الجنيد | reports | Junayd says the people of Paradise do not subsist through God's own uncreated subsistence; rather, they are made to subsist by it, since only God has eternally remained and will remain in truth.

[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:44:53-56/r5] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The only death they have tasted is the first death they experienced in worldly life; they do not die in Paradise.

[BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The exception means excepting the first death already tasted in worldly life; illa is used in the sense of apart from or after, as at 4:22. | mentions 4:22
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · قيل | reports | Another explanation says the blessed meet the spirit and fragrant provision and see their Paradise homes at death, so their worldly death resembles being in Paradise through contact with its causes and vision of it.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p237#2/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | God protects them from the punishment of Hell.

[TABRISI:44:56-59/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Death is likened to unpleasant food that one tastes, then denied for Paradise's people.
[TABRISI:44:56-59/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Though all afterlife inhabitants avoid death, this reassurance singles out the blessed to promise pleasant life; those enduring deathlike punishment undergo repeated deaths from torment.
[TABRISI:44:56-59/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | One interpretation takes the exception to mean “after the first death.”
[TABRISI:44:56-59/r5] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Another interpretation means that they have already tasted the first death.
[TABRISI:44:56-59/r6] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | prefers | The remaining interpretation means “other than the first death”; al-Tabrisi's grammatical explanation is in the preceding segment.
[TABRISI:44:56-59/r7] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | God keeps them away from the punishment of the Fire.
[TABRISI:44:56-59/r8] TABRISI, d. 548 · المعتزلة | reports | The Mu'tazila argue that a sinful believer cannot leave Hell, since this verse says the saved people are protected from the Fire.
[TABRISI:44:56-59/r9] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | rejects | It may concern those who do not deserve entry, those pardoned despite deserving it, or protection forever or from the kind of torment reserved for unbelievers.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الفراء والزجاج | reports | Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj take illa to mean “apart from”: the people of Paradise taste no death other than the death they experienced in this world. | mentions 4:22, 11:107

[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p351#3/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن جرير | reports | Ibn Jarir takes illa to mean “after,” as in one interpretation of 4:22. | mentions 4:22
[RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After describing their pleasures and comforts, God states that their life in paradise is everlasting.

[RAZI-FULL:v27p217/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Another explanation takes illā as meaning but: they do not taste death there, but they have already tasted the first death.
